Thresholds of a cumulative link fit

Source: R/ilm_ordinal.R, R/zzz-iml-aliases.R
ilm_thresholds.Rd

The cut points on the latent scale, with their standard errors. There are J - 1 of them for J categories and they are increasing by construction: the fit estimates the first and the logarithms of the gaps, so an ordering violation is not something the optimiser can reach.

Usage

ilm_thresholds(object, level = 0.95)

Arguments

object

A fitted ilm_model() with an ordinal family.

level

Confidence level.

Value

A data frame of cut, estimate, se, lower and upper.

Details

Read them against the linear predictor, which is subtracted: P(Y <= j) = F(threshold_j - eta). A positive coefficient therefore pushes probability towards the higher categories.

See also

ilm_check_proportional() for the assumption that makes one coefficient per predictor enough.

Examples

set.seed(1); n <- 400
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n))
z <- 0.8 * d$x + rlogis(n)
d$y <- factor(cut(z, c(-Inf, -1, 1, Inf), labels = c("lo", "mid", "hi")),
              ordered = TRUE)
f <- ilm_model(y ~ x, data = d, family = "ordinal", verbose = FALSE)
ilm_thresholds(f)
#>      cut   estimate        se      lower      upper
#> 1 lo|mid -0.7810335 0.1112162 -0.9990132 -0.5630538
#> 2 mid|hi  0.9322873 0.1138474  0.7091505  1.1554241
